holidays.name: National Pecan Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the buttery, nutty pecan by baking pies, tossing them into salads, or just snacking straight from the bag. Pecan lovers get to argue about whether it's pronounced 'pee-can' or 'pi-kahn' with extra enthusiasm.
holidays.origin: Pecan Day is an unofficial food observance that is popular among food-calendar enthusiasts and nut growers. Pecans are the only major tree nut native to North America, and the day honors their long agricultural history in the southern United States.
holidays.funFact: The word 'pecan' comes from an Algonquian word meaning 'a nut requiring a stone to crack.' Pecan is also the official state nut of Texas, and pecan trees can live and produce nuts for over 300 years.

holidays.name: National Gardening Day
holidays.description: A day for people to dig in the dirt, plant seeds, and pretend they will definitely remember to water everything. Gardeners and houseplant killers alike are encouraged to get outside and grow something.
holidays.origin: National Gardening Day is an unofficial observance that falls in mid-April, when spring planting season is getting underway across much of the Northern Hemisphere. It encourages people to start gardens and appreciate green spaces.
holidays.funFact: Gardening is often credited with reducing stress, and some studies suggest that a soil bacterium called Mycobacterium vaccae may boost serotonin levels, so dirt may literally be a mood booster.

holidays.name: Ex-Spouse Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day dedicated to acknowledging the people you used to be married to. You can send a kind note, bury the hatchet, or simply be thankful for the lessons learned, and for the fact that you no longer have to share a bathroom.
holidays.origin: Ex-Spouse Day is an informal, humorous observance listed on many quirky holiday calendars. It's meant to encourage civility and maturity between former partners, especially those who co-parent.
holidays.funFact: Many holiday calendars list it alongside other mid-April oddities, and it is often used as a prompt for people to practice the art of the polite, non-passive-aggressive text message.

holidays.name: International Moment of Laughter Day
holidays.description: A day to stop everything and laugh, whether it's from a joke, a silly video, or sheer absurdity. It's about letting out a good chuckle to lighten the mood and share joy with everyone around you.
holidays.origin: Established by Izzy Gesell, a humorist and educator, International Moment of Laughter Day was created to promote the health and social benefits of laughter, and it is celebrated on April 14 in many places.
holidays.funFact: Laughter is contagious for real: the brain's premotor cortex responds to the sound of laughter by prepping facial muscles to smile along, which is why a laugh track works even when the jokes don't.

holidays.name: Look Up at the Sky Day
holidays.description: A day that asks you to put down your phone and tilt your head back to admire clouds, birds, stars, and whatever else is going on overhead. It's a free, zero-equipment holiday that is easy to celebrate.
holidays.origin: This lighthearted observance is credited to sky-watching enthusiasts and listed on quirky holiday calendars as a reminder to slow down and notice the sky, a fitting activity for spring weather.
holidays.funFact: Cloud watchers have a name: 'nephophiles.' The Cloud Appreciation Society has tens of thousands of members worldwide who gather to celebrate the beauty of clouds.
